overview: Allied Farmers is a small NZX-listed rural investment company and asset manager, now built around 100%-owned New Zealand Rural Land Management (NZRLM), the external manager of NZX-listed New Zealand Rural Land Company (NZL). Following the December 2025 sale of its 67.8%-owned livestock agency, NZ Farmers Livestock (NZFL), to Rural Livestock Ltd, Allied has transformed from a diversified rural operator into a focused, capital-light rural fund manager sitting on a large legacy tax-loss pool and cash from the NZFL divestment awaiting redeployment. The company operates solely within New Zealand.

business_model.summary: Historically a mix of livestock agency commissions/trading (NZFL, sold Dec-2025) and recurring asset-management fees (NZRLM). Post-sale, revenue is now overwhelmingly NZRLM management, transaction and performance fees earned from managing NZL's rural land portfolio (forestry, pastoral, horticultural, dairy), plus interest income on cash/loan advances and an investment property acquired via a distressed-mortgagee transaction. Management is exploring redeployment of ~NZ$7.5m NZFL sale proceeds into new rural investments to utilise ~NZ$172-175m of carried-forward tax losses.

revenue_streams.name: Livestock Services (NZFL agency, veal export) - DIVESTED Dec-2025
Rural Land Management (NZRLM fees from NZL: ~0.5% AUM monitoring fee, 1.25% transaction fee, NAV-linked performance fee paid in NZL shares)
Financial Services (livestock finance referrals to Heartland Bank) - largely divested with NZFL
Parent Operations (interest income, investment property rental, loan advances)

business_model.note_on_mix: Percentages reflect FY2025 (year to 30 June 2025) segment income before the Dec-2025 NZFL divestment; FY2026 (current year) revenue mix will be overwhelmingly NZRLM management fees plus interest/investment income from redeployed NZFL sale proceeds, since NZFL is now reported as discontinued operations.
business_model.customer_type: B2B/institutional - NZRLM's sole material client is NZL (NZX-listed) and its Australian co-investor Roc Partners; historically NZFL served farmer/agency clients (B2B/B2C hybrid)

main_competitors: Rural Livestock Limited (acquirer of NZFL, national livestock agency competitor)
NZX/Craigs-advised rural land funds and syndicators
Direct farm ownership/family farming as the alternative to institutional rural land vehicles
competitive_position.market_position: Niche, sub-scale player. NZRLM is the sole contracted manager of NZL (one of very few NZX-listed rural land vehicles), giving it a monopoly-like position over that specific mandate, but NZL itself is small relative to NZ's total rural land market. Post-NZFL sale, Allied has no operating scale business of its own.

moat_factors.description: NZRLM holds exclusive, long-dated management agreements with NZL and Roc Partners; switching managers would be disruptive and costly for NZL, creating some stickiness, but the mandate is renewable/terminable and concentrated with a single client

~NZ$172-175m of unrecognised carried-forward tax losses (from the 2009 Hanover Finance collapse) shelters future NZ profits from tax for years, materially boosting after-tax returns on any redeployed capital, subject to shareholder continuity rules
Managing Director Richard Milsom co-founded NZRLM/NZL and holds ~15.8% of Allied Farmers, aligning incentives with NZRLM's success
Long operating history in NZ rural finance and asset management provides credibility with landowners and co-investors

weaknesses: Extreme customer concentration - NZRLM's revenue is almost entirely dependent on one client relationship (NZL/Roc Partners)
Very small scale (market cap roughly NZ$20-25m) with thin trading liquidity and high shareholder concentration (top 2 holders own ~32%)
No dividend paid since FY2020 (one-off 1.2cps) - policy of retaining all earnings to preserve/utilise tax losses, limiting appeal to income investors
Loss of NZFL removes a scaled, diversified operating cash-generative business, leaving Allied dependent on successfully redeploying capital into new, as-yet-unidentified investments
Complex, related-party-heavy corporate structure (SPVs, non-trading subsidiaries, NZFL/Redshaw minority interests) can obscure underlying economics

growth_drivers: Redeployment of ~NZ$7.5m+ NZFL sale proceeds (with further ~NZ$2.4m received in H2 FY2026) into new rural sector investments or loans that utilise the large tax loss pool
Growth in NZRLM's fee base as NZL grows its land portfolio (17,000+ hectares) via further acquisitions, including the March 2025 Canterbury dairy farm purchase funded partly via asset recycling
NZL's re-commencement of dividends in FY25 signals improving NZL portfolio performance, which flows through to NZRLM's NAV-linked performance fees
Potential new SPV-style structured transactions (e.g. the Sept-2024 Waikato property/MC Redlands deal) using ring-fenced financing to deploy capital with limited recourse to the parent
Rural loan book/private credit opportunities (e.g. the South Canterbury dairy farm working-capital loan) as a diversification of Allied's asset management skillset
Cyclical upswing in NZ livestock/dairy prices (benefited the now-divested NZFL through FY25 and into FY26) supports the broader rural land and lending backdrop NZRLM/Allied operates in

business.description: NZRLM's fee income is dependent almost entirely on its management contracts with NZL/Roc Partners; loss or renegotiation of this mandate would eliminate most of Allied's ongoing revenue
With NZFL sold, Allied must find new investments for ~NZ$10m+ of cash; poor capital allocation decisions (as seen historically with the Hanover-era finance book) could destroy value
Divesting NZFL removes a proven, cash-generative operating business, leaving a smaller, more concentrated entity

business.risk: Veal/livestock segment volatility (residual exposure via transitional arrangements)
business.description: Softening skin prices and feeder-calf tally pressures affected the veal business pre-sale; any earn-out or completion adjustments tied to NZFL performance carry residual risk

financial.description: The MC Redlands Pty Ltd financing (NZ$10.5m nominal, fair-valued through P&L) tied to the Waikato property SPV introduces mark-to-market earnings volatility (NZ$928k fair value loss in FY25) and interest rate/property value sensitivity

Total liabilities grew from NZ$14.6m (FY24) to NZ$27.6m (FY25), including new term loans and Heartland Bank borrowings; while non-recourse to the parent in the SPV structure, headline gearing has increased
Market capitalisation of roughly NZ$20-25m and thin free float create wide bid-ask spreads and valuation volatility for shareholders seeking to enter/exit

regulatory.description: The ~NZ$172-175m tax loss asset is contingent on maintaining shareholder continuity under NZ tax law; the Board amended the constitution in 2024 and obtained an NZX waiver to restrict share transfers/ownership thresholds specifically to protect this asset - a breach would permanently forfeit a major source of value

regulatory.risk: NZX Major Transaction / continuous disclosure requirements
regulatory.description: Significant transactions (e.g. NZFL sale) require shareholder approval as Major Transactions under NZX Listing Rule 5.1.1(a), adding process risk/delay to strategic moves

macro.description: NZRLM's performance fees are directly linked to NZL's portfolio NAV, which is sensitive to NZ rural land values, interest rates and farm profitability
Variable-rate Heartland Bank borrowings (7.32% at FY25) and the cost-of-debt assumptions underlying the MC Redlands fair-valued liability are sensitive to NZ interest rate movements
While NZFL is divested, Allied's remaining rural loan exposures (e.g. South Canterbury dairy farm loan) and NZL's tenant farm profitability remain linked to milk payouts and livestock prices

macro_factors.industry_outlook: NZ agriculture is in a cyclical upswing as of FY25/FY26 - livestock and dairy prices at multi-year highs, farmer confidence improved, and NZL resuming dividends - supportive of both rural land valuations (NZRLM's fee base) and any new rural lending Allied undertakes
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate to high - underlying NZ rural asset values and livestock/dairy trading conditions are cyclical, though NZRLM's fixed monitoring fee component provides some stability versus the now-divested NZFL trading business
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - variable rate bank debt, fair-valued structured financing, and land-value-linked performance fees are all sensitive to NZ interest rate moves and the OCR cycle
key_input_costs: N/A directly (fee/asset-management model) - indirectly, NZ rural land values, livestock prices, and milk solids payouts drive the earnings base Allied is exposed to

recent_developments.event: Allied Farmers (via SPV) acquired Waikato land/buildings for NZ$10.5m from a mortgagee, funded via a ring-fenced, non-recourse structured loan; also advanced a NZ$3m working-capital loan to a South Canterbury dairy operation
Announced conditional sale of NZ Farmers Livestock (NZFL) to Rural Livestock Ltd for an enterprise value of ~NZ$10.988m, subject to shareholder approval as a Major Transaction

FY2025 annual result: NPAT attributable to shareholders of NZ$2.871m (FY24: NZ$5.206m), EPS 9.97cps (FY24: 18.07cps); decline driven by non-repeat of FY24's one-off NZ$4.2m Frankton saleyards gain, offset by materially improved underlying NZFL trading
Sale of NZFL to Rural Livestock Ltd completed; Allied's 67.8% share of proceeds ~NZ$7.5m+ cash, with a further ~NZ$2.4m expected in H2 FY2026 from completion adjustments

HY2026 (six months to 31 Dec 2025) result: consolidated profit after tax of NZ$3.542m (+44.75% YoY), largely reflecting NZFL divestment gain and tax benefits; continuing operations (ex-NZFL) posted a net loss before tax of NZ$0.517m, reflecting the now much smaller cost base without NZFL's operating earnings; profit attributable to shareholders NZ$3.817m, EPS 13.25cps
Received further ~NZ$2.40m from NZFL sale completion adjustments

NZL (managed by NZRLM) recommenced shareholder dividends during FY25 after a suspension, and acquired a 305ha high-yielding Canterbury dairy farm in March 2025, funded partly by selling two pastoral farms - generating transaction and recurring fees for NZRLM

guidance.as_of: HY2026 result (27 February 2026) / FY2025 Annual Report (29 September 2025)

items.notes: Board continues policy of paying no dividend to preserve and utilise the ~NZ$172-175m tax loss pool by deploying earnings into growth opportunities; Board has indicated it would consider returning capital if suitable investment opportunities do not emerge

items.target: Redeploy ~NZ$7.5-10m of NZFL sale proceeds into new rural sector investments/loans
items.notes: No specific quantitative revenue/earnings target given; strategy is to grow the rural asset management business (NZRLM) and pursue complementary investment opportunities that utilise tax losses

items.target: NZRLM to achieve NPBT 10% higher than FY25 NPAT (25% weighting) plus strategy/transaction/leadership objectives (75% weighting)
items.notes: Internal incentive target only, not public earnings guidance; reflects management's internal expectation of NZRLM growth

guidance.management_commentary: Chair Shelley Ruha noted FY25/early FY26 trading conditions for the (now divested) livestock business were the most buoyant in years, with cattle and sheep prices at elevated levels, though flagged uncertainty from US tariffs and geopolitical developments. Post NZFL sale, management's stated focus is on growing NZRLM's asset management business and evaluating new complementary rural investment opportunities for the freed-up capital, with no formal quantitative revenue or earnings guidance issued for FY2026 given the business transition.

bull_case: Large uncrystallised tax loss asset (~NZ$172-175m) shelters future profits from NZ tax, materially enhancing after-tax returns on any capital Allied redeploys

Post-NZFL sale, Allied is now a leaner, capital-light asset manager (NZRLM) with a fresh ~NZ$10m cash pile to redeploy into higher-return opportunities, with the potential removal of a lower-margin, working-capital-intensive trading business

NZRLM's fee base (monitoring, transaction and NAV-linked performance fees) benefits directly from growth in NZL's rural land portfolio and NZ rural land value appreciation, providing a scalable, largely fixed-cost fee stream
Management (Richard Milsom) co-founded NZRLM/NZL and holds a meaningful personal stake (~15.8%), aligning incentives with growing the asset management franchise
Favourable NZ agricultural cycle (strong livestock/dairy prices, NZL resuming dividends) supports both near-term NZRLM performance fees and the broader environment for redeploying sale proceeds
bear_case: Extreme customer concentration - NZRLM's income is dependent on a single management relationship with NZL/Roc Partners; any renegotiation, termination or underperformance of that mandate would severely impair earnings

No clear reinvestment plan yet disclosed for NZFL sale proceeds; history of value destruction in prior capital allocation decisions (Hanover Finance-era losses that created the tax loss pool in the first place) raises execution risk
Zero dividends since a single 1.2cps payment in FY2020; shareholders receive no cash return and must rely entirely on capital growth/successful reinvestment, which is unproven post-transition
Very small market cap (~NZ$20-25m) with concentrated share register (top 2 holders ~32%) and thin liquidity limit institutional interest and can produce volatile, wide-spread pricing
Continuing operations (ex-NZFL) posted a net loss before tax in HY2026, showing the residual cost base is not yet covered by NZRLM fee income alone, until new investments are deployed
